**We charge $35.**

- Patients must cancel at least 48 hours before their appointment [3], so a 24-hour cancellation counts as a late cancellation.
- The late cancellation fee for a hygiene appointment, such as a cleaning, is **$35** [1].

**Exceptions:**
- **Once-a-year waiver:** The front desk can waive the fee once per patient per calendar year. If you do, note the waiver in the patient's account notes [1].
- **Always waived:** Medical emergencies and county-declared severe weather [1].
The office is at 410 Heron Lake Blvd, Suite 200, Kissimmee, FL 34741 [1].

**SunCoast patient: Yes.** SunCoast PPO covers 2 cleanings per calendar year with no 6-month spacing rule [1][4]. Since May 1 was this patient's first cleaning of the year, an October 1 cleaning would be their second and should be covered [1].

**BlueWave patient: Not covered on October 1.** BlueWave Dental HMO allows 2 cleanings per year but requires them to be at least 6 months apart [4][1]. May 1 to October 1 is only 5 months.
- The earliest covered date would be on or after November 1, which is 6 months after May 1 [4].
- If the patient still wants October 1, tell them the self-pay fee before booking. For an adult cleaning, that fee is $120 [1].

**Reminder:** Always check the patient's insurance frequency rule before booking the recall appointment [3].

**Charge $35.**

- A patient more than 15 minutes late for a hygiene visit must be rescheduled unless the provider agrees to see them [1].
- A late arrival that has to be rescheduled counts as a late cancellation, and the late cancellation fee applies [1].
- The late cancellation fee for a hygiene appointment is **$35** [3].

**Exceptions:**
- You may waive the fee once per patient per calendar year at your discretion. If you do, note the waiver in the patient's account notes [3].
- Always waive the fee if the lateness was due to a medical emergency or county-declared severe weather [3].

*Note: This assumes the cleaning is booked as a hygiene appointment. If it was booked as a doctor visit, the fee would be $50 [3].*
I don't know, please check with the office manager. None of the available sources list a price for teeth whitening.

The main phone number for Lakeside Family Dental is **(407) 555-0142** [3].

The front desk doesn't answer phones from 12:00 PM to 1:00 PM Monday through Thursday. Calls during that time go to voicemail and are returned by 1:30 PM [1].

On Fridays, the office is open **7:30 AM to 1:00 PM** [1].

On the **last Friday of each month**, the office closes early at **11:00 AM** for the staff meeting [3].

The no-show fee is **$75**. A no-show is when the patient doesn't arrive and doesn't call [1].

- **Waivers:** The front desk may waive the fee once per patient per calendar year. If you do, note the waiver in the patient's account notes [1]. Fees are always waived for medical emergencies and county-declared severe weather [1].
- **Patients under 18:** The fee is charged to the responsible party on the account [2].
- **Missed confirmations:** Not receiving or missing a confirmation text does not excuse a no-show [4].
- **Repeat no-shows:** After three no-shows within 12 months, the patient may only book same-day appointments for the next 6 months, unless the office manager approves an exception [3].

Under the three-strike rule, **three** no-shows within 12 months trigger the restriction [1]. After that, the patient may only book **same-day appointments for the next 6 months** [1]. Any exception must be approved by the office manager [1].

New patients should arrive **15 minutes early** for their first visit [1]. If they haven't completed the digital intake packet, they'll be given a tablet in the waiting room to finish it [1]. We'll also scan their photo ID and insurance card if they weren't uploaded beforehand [1].

The Lakeside Smile Club costs **$29 per month or $299 per year** [2]. It's an in-house membership for patients without insurance [2].

It includes:
- 2 cleanings, 2 exams, and 1 set of bitewing X-rays per year [2]
- 20% off other treatment [2]

For an in-house payment plan, the down payment is **25%** of the treatment cost [1][2]. The remaining balance can be split over a **maximum of 6 months**, interest free [1][2].

These plans are available for treatment over $500 [1][2]. For treatment over $3,000, patients are referred to our financing partner, BrightPay Health, which offers 12 to 24 month plans [1].

Records requests must be fulfilled within **15 business days** [1]. Patients request their records using the Records Release Form [1].

A few related details:
- Electronic copies (secure email or patient portal) are free. Paper copies cost $0.50 per page after the first 10 pages [1].
- X-rays are provided digitally on request [1].
- If the records are going to another office, a signed release from the patient (or parent/guardian for minors) must be on file before anything is faxed or emailed [2].

The after-hours voicemail gives the on-call doctor's pager number: **(407) 555-0177** [1]. The on-call doctor rotates weekly between Dr. Ruiz and Dr. Bell [1].

If a patient has swelling that affects breathing or swallowing, a high fever with facial swelling, or a jaw injury from an accident, tell them to go to the emergency room or call 911 [4].

They should come in **within 60 minutes** [1]. A knocked-out permanent tooth counts as a dental emergency [3].

Until they arrive, they should:
- Pick the tooth up by the crown, not the root [1].
- Rinse it gently [1].
- Try to put it back in the socket, or keep it in milk [1].

A minor aged **14 to 17** may attend a routine cleaning without a parent, as long as a signed **Minor Attendance Form** is on file [1].

A few conditions apply:
- This applies only to routine cleanings **after the first visit**. A parent or guardian must be present for the first visit [1][4].
- A parent or guardian must also be present for any treatment involving numbing, extractions, or sedation [1].
- Patients under 18 need a parent or legal guardian to sign consent forms [1].
The SunCoast Dental PPO annual maximum is **$1,500 per person** [1].

You have **90 days from the date of service** to file a SunCoast Dental PPO claim [1][2]. However, office procedure is to submit claims electronically **the same day** as the appointment [1], using payer ID **SCD01** [2].

A BlueWave Dental HMO patient's copay for a porcelain crown (D2740) is **$450** [1].

Before the visit, confirm on the BlueWave portal that the patient is still assigned to Lakeside Family Dental [3]. If they aren't, the plan will not pay [1].

No, Lakeside Family Dental is **out of network** with GuardStar Dental PPO [1]. Patients with GuardStar can still be seen [1].

For GuardStar patients:
- GuardStar pays the **patient** directly for out-of-network claims, not the office [4].
- The full fee is collected at the time of service, and the patient receives a claim form to submit [4].

The lab (Coastline Dental Lab) has a standard turnaround of **10 business days** after the scan is sent [2]. Because of this, the seat appointment is booked **2 weeks** after the prep visit, and the office confirms the crown has arrived from the lab 2 days before that appointment [1].

Bill the crown (D2740) on the **seat date**, not the prep date [1]. Insurance pays on the date the crown is permanently placed [1].

The seat appointment is booked **2 weeks** after the prep [2].

The self-pay price for bitewing X-rays is **$65** [1]. If a patient's insurance won't pay because of frequency limits, we tell them this cost before taking the X-rays [1].

Patients without insurance can also join the Lakeside Smile Club for $29 per month or $299 per year. Membership includes 1 set of bitewing X-rays per year, plus 2 cleanings, 2 exams, and 20% off other treatment [3].
Nitrous oxide (laughing gas) costs $55 per visit [1]. If you need IV sedation instead, we refer you to a partner oral surgeon [1].

If a new patient's blood pressure is **above 180/110**, we do not provide treatment that day and refer the patient to their physician [2]. The hygienist takes the blood pressure while reviewing the patient's medical history at the start of the new patient exam [2].

Use **D2392** for a two-surface MO filling on a back tooth. Don't use D2391, which is for one surface only [1].

- D2392 is a tooth-colored filling, two surfaces, back tooth [1].
- The claim must include the tooth number and surfaces (here, M and O) [1].
- The self-pay office fee is $235 [1].

The sources only list codes for **tooth-colored** fillings. If this is a silver (amalgam) filling, I don't know the code. Please check with the office manager.

Both D4341 and D4342 are deep cleanings (scaling and root planing). The difference is **how many teeth in the quadrant** are treated:

- **D4341:** 4 or more teeth in a quadrant [1]. The self-pay fee is $245 per quadrant [1].
- **D4342:** 1 to 3 teeth in a quadrant [1]. The self-pay fee is $175 per quadrant [1].

**What they have in common:**
- Both require the quadrant on the claim: UR, UL, LR, or LL [1].
- Claims for either code need perio charting showing pockets of 4 mm or more, plus recent X-rays [1].
- Most insurers allow either code once per quadrant every 24 months [1].
- After a deep cleaning, the patient moves to periodontal maintenance (D4910) every 3 months [1].
- A patient with active gum disease needs D4341 or D4342 before a regular adult cleaning (D1110) [4].

The total self-pay office fee is **$1,545**: $1,250 for the crown plus $295 for the buildup [1].

Since the treatment is over $500, the patient can use our in-house payment plan: 25% down, with the balance paid over up to 6 months [2].
The office is open on the **first and third Saturday of each month only**, from 8:00 AM to 12:00 PM [1]. Saturday hours are for **hygiene appointments only** [1].

Two plans require 6 months between cleanings:

- **BlueWave Dental HMO** requires 6 months between cleanings [1]. Its plan summary confirms 2 cleanings per year, at least 6 months apart [4].
- **SunState Kids** also requires 6 months between cleanings [1].

**SunCoast PPO** works differently. It counts 2 cleanings per calendar year rather than requiring 6 months between them [1][4].

If a cleaning won't be covered, tell the patient the self-pay fee ($120 for an adult cleaning) before booking [1].

The sources don't confirm whether these plans are in-network or list all of our in-network plans. For a complete list, please check with the office manager.

**SunCoast Dental PPO** covers a full-mouth or panoramic X-ray **once every 5 years** [2].

**BlueWave Dental HMO** covers full-mouth X-rays **once every 3 years** [1].

So BlueWave allows one two years sooner than SunCoast. Note that SunCoast's limit covers full-mouth *or* panoramic X-rays together [2]. If the plan won't pay, tell the patient the self-pay cost before taking the X-ray: $145 for a full-mouth series [3].

Under **SunCoast Dental PPO**, a crown on the same tooth can be replaced **once every 5 years** [1].

Under **GuardStar Dental PPO**, a crown on the same tooth can be replaced **once every 7 years** [2].

So SunCoast allows replacement two years sooner than GuardStar.

Lakeside Family Dental is in network with these plans:

- **SunCoast Dental PPO** [1]
- **BlueWave Dental HMO** [1]
- **SunState Kids program** [1]

Patients with other insurance plans are seen as out of network [1]. For example, Lakeside is out of network with GuardStar Dental PPO, but GuardStar patients can still be seen [3].

SunCoast Dental PPO has a **$50 per-person deductible** (with a $150 family maximum), and the deductible is waived for preventive care [2]. GuardStar Dental PPO has a **$75 per-person deductible** [1].

So SunCoast's per-person deductible is $25 lower than GuardStar's.

Lakeside Family Dental is in network with SunCoast [2] but out of network with GuardStar [1].

**SunCoast Dental PPO** covers **1 set of bitewing X-rays per calendar year** [3].

**GuardStar Dental PPO** covers **1 set of bitewing X-rays every 2 years** for adults [2].

GuardStar covers bitewings half as often as SunCoast.

**Also good to know:**
- Our office default for adults is bitewings every 12 months, or every 24 months for low-risk adults [1].
- Always check the patient's insurance frequency limits before taking X-rays. If the plan won't pay, tell the patient the self-pay cost first, which is $65 for bitewings [1].
- Lakeside Family Dental is out of network with GuardStar, though patients may still be seen [4].

**Yes, a pre-authorization is needed, for two reasons:**

1. **SunCoast PPO requires it** for any single treatment over $400 [2]. A $1,250 crown is well above that.
2. **Our office policy requires it** for any treatment plan over $1,000 with any insurance, even if the insurer doesn't, so the patient knows their cost [2].

Also, when an insured patient asks about crown cost, we offer a pre-authorization and never guess [1]. Note that $1,250 is our self-pay price, and a buildup adds $295 if needed [1].

**Next steps:**
- The doctor finalizes the treatment plan in ChairSide PM [4].
- Submit the pre-authorization electronically with the same attachments a claim would need [4].
- Tell the patient most insurers respond within 2 to 4 weeks [4].
- When the response arrives, call the patient to review their estimated cost and schedule [4].
- At the crown prep visit, the team confirms pre-authorization status and the estimated cost before starting [3].

**Exception:** If the treatment is urgent (infection or severe pain), it does not wait for the pre-authorization. The doctor documents the urgency in the chart [4].

Yes, we still send a pre-authorization.

- **BlueWave doesn't require it here.** BlueWave HMO only requires pre-authorization for specialist referrals [1].
- **Our office policy does.** We send a pre-authorization for any treatment plan over $1,000 with any insurance, even when the insurer doesn't require it, so the patient knows their cost [1]. At $1,200, this plan qualifies.

**Next steps:**
1. Make sure the doctor has finalized the treatment plan in ChairSide PM [2].
2. Submit the pre-authorization electronically with the same attachments a claim would need [2].
3. Tell the patient most insurers respond within 2 to 4 weeks [2].
4. When the response arrives, call the patient to review their estimated cost and schedule [2].

If any of the treatment is urgent (infection, severe pain), it doesn't wait for the pre-authorization. The doctor documents the urgency in the chart [2].

**No, not to SunState Kids.** Porcelain crowns on back teeth are not covered; a **stainless steel crown** is covered instead [3]. Covered services have no copays or deductibles [3].

Before the visit:
- **Confirm the patient is under 21.** We only accept SunState Kids for patients under 21 [3].
- **Check eligibility on the day of the visit**, since coverage can end in any month [3].
- **Bill on the seat date.** Crowns are billed on the day the crown is permanently placed, not the prep date [4].

If the family wants a porcelain crown anyway, the sources don't say whether we can charge them privately for it under this program. I don't know, please check with the office manager.

Yes. SunCoast Dental PPO covers fluoride for patients **under age 16**, so a 15-year-old qualifies [2]. It's covered **twice per year** [2].

When billing, use code D1206 (fluoride varnish), and check the plan's age limit (under 16 for SunCoast) [4].

The sources don't say what percentage SunCoast pays for fluoride. The plan lists preventive care as "exams, cleanings, X-rays" at 100% but doesn't name fluoride [3]. For the exact cost to the patient, please check with the office manager.

Before the patient sees an oral surgeon, **BlueWave must approve a referral, and the approval has to come before the appointment** [1]. Approval takes **5 to 7 business days** [1], so schedule the oral surgeon appointment far enough out to allow for it.

**It depends on whether we're out-of-network with GuardStar for this patient. Our sources don't say, so please confirm that first.**

**If we're out-of-network:**
- Collect the full $400 at the time of service [1].
- Give the patient a claim form. GuardStar pays the patient directly for out-of-network claims, not the office [1].

**If we're in-network:**
- The sources don't cover GuardStar's in-network handling. Under our general policy, we collect the estimated patient portion at the time of service, based on insurance verification [3].
- We bill any difference after insurance pays [3].

**Other notes:**
- GuardStar has no waiting periods, so coverage timing shouldn't be an issue [1].
- This patient can't use a payment plan, because we offer those only for treatment over $500 [4].

If you can't confirm our network status with GuardStar, I don't know, please check with the office manager.

**Other things to mention:**
- **If the patient has insurance:** Our office requires a pre-treatment estimate for any treatment plan over $1,000, so the patient knows their cost before committing [4].
- **If the patient doesn't have insurance:** Suggest they ask about the Lakeside Smile Club [2]. The sources don't give details on how it works or whether it lowers the cost.

**What to do:**

- **Book the next emergency slot today.** Pain of 7 or higher qualifies for a same-day emergency appointment, even without swelling [1].
- **Finish the triage questions** to make sure nothing more urgent is going on [3]:
  - Which tooth or area hurts, and since when?
  - Do you have a fever?
  - Does the pain wake you up at night or linger after hot or cold?
- **Send them to the ER or have them call 911 instead** if any of these come up [1][2]:
  - Swelling that affects breathing or swallowing
  - High fever with facial swelling
  - A jaw injury from an accident
- **Don't diagnose or recommend prescription medicine** over the phone. Only the doctor can do that [1].
